title: The Bird Let Loose in Eastern Skies
description: The Bird Let Loose in Eastern Skies in Tonic Solfa to ST. PETER, doh is Eb: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: Thomas Moore wrote these words. They were printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 451 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “Heaven Desired”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Common Metre (8.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to ST. PETER; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: The bird let loose in East-ern skies, Re-turn-ing fond-ly home, Ne'er stoops to earth her wing, nor flies Where id-le war-blers roam.

lines: The bird let loose in Eastern skies,
Ne'er stoops to earth her wing, nor flies
But high she shoots through air and light —
Where nothing earthly bounds her flight,
So grant me, God, from every snare
To hold my course to thee.
No sin to cloud, no lure to stay
My soul, as home she springs;
Thy sunshine on her joyful way,

licence: Public domain: Thomas Moore died in 1852.
credits: Words by Thomas Moore (1779–1852), public domain, as printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion (1853); set to ST. PETER by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
